convention: Cube. Each of the 6 square faces carries one engraved digit, identified via connected-component clustering (weld-by-position + BFS-by-triangle) on the Antique_Gold_UV_PBR material (D6_primitive1, 3351 verts), separated from the die body (Dice_Recess_BlackRed_UV_PBR, D6_primitive0, 24 verts -- tiny trim, same split pattern as D8/D12). connectedComponents('D6_primitive1') yields 13 components: 1 body-shell component (component 0, 1247 verts, centroid ~origin) + 6 small decorative corner-stud components (56-64 verts each, one per face, direction proxies only, normal/centroid exactly axis-aligned in local space) + 6 large digit-glyph components (207-344 verts each, one per face). Glyph/stud pairs grouped by matching local-space axis direction: glyph7+stud6=+Y, glyph8+stud1=-X, glyph9+stud2=-Z, glyph10+stud4=+Z, glyph11+stud3=+X, glyph12+stud5=-Y. CRITICAL ASSET-SPECIFIC CAVEAT (same family as D8/D12): the glTF root node (__root__) carries a non-identity transform (rotationQuaternion [0,1,0,0] = 180 deg around Y, plus scaling [1,1,-1] = mirror on Z). On top of that, D6_primitive1 itself (the mesh actually rendered) combines with this root transform into a composite world matrix that includes a near-identity-but-NOT-identity rotation (slight tilt, roughly quaternion-equivalent to [0.0384, 0.0225, -0.0609, 0.9972], i.e. a few degrees of tilt on all 3 axes) plus uniform scaling ~0.8914-0.8954 on the diagonal. The local-space axis directions ([1,0,0], [0,1,0], [0,0,1], etc.) are NOT the correct camera-aim directions for this asset -- they must be transformed via BABYLON.Vector3.TransformNormal(localDir, mesh.getWorldMatrix()) first. The LOCAL-space normal/centroid-direction values recorded below are what a runtime consumer reading mesh.getVerticesData(NormalKind) or raw local positions (matching src/dice/procedural.ts convention) will see; they are NOT what should be fed directly to a camera for a human/vision-model screenshot check on this asset -- always transform through the world matrix first.

mesh_notes.D6_primitive0: Dice_Recess_BlackRed_UV_PBR material, 24 vertices -- body/recess trim, not a face.
mesh_notes.D6_primitive1: Antique_Gold_UV_PBR material, 3351 vertices -- body shell (component 0, 1247 verts, centroid at origin) + 6 small corner-stud decorative components (56-64 verts each, one per face, direction proxies only) + 6 large digit-glyph components (207-344 verts each, one per face) -- confirmed by screenshot+vision reading of each of the 6 glyph components independently, with centroid-projection verification (see validation_notes) before every read.

validation_notes: THIS IS A REMAPEAMENTO (re-mapping) that CORRECTS a confirmed error in the previous D6 mapping. ROOT CAUSE OF THE OLD ERROR: the D6 was the FIRST die mapped in this phase, before any subagent had discovered that ALL 7 glTFs in this PolyhedralDice asset family carry a non-trivial transform on top of the (expected) root-node 180-deg-Y + Z-mirror transform shared with D8/D12/D20 -- specifically, D6's own primitive/node combines into a world matrix with a small but non-zero additional rotation (several degrees of tilt on each axis) plus uniform scale ~0.89, not identity. The old mapping pointed the camera directly at the RAW LOCAL-SPACE axis vector (e.g. pointCameraAtNormal(1,0,0,4) with no world-matrix transform), which shows the WRONG face for this asset. Critically, the SUM-7 invariant and the complete-set-{1..6}-no-repeats invariant BOTH still passed on the old (wrong) mapping, because the error was a CONSISTENT SWAP of an opposite-axis pair (X and Z axes were swapped as a pair: old +X=2/-X=5/+Z=3/-Z=4 vs the correct +X=5/-X=2/+Z=4/-Z=3) -- a paired swap preserves both invariants, so neither caught the bug. +Y=1/-Y=6 happened to already be correct in the old mapping and is reconfirmed here. METHOD USED HERE (matches the validated D8/D10/D12/D20 method): (1) Loaded D6.gltf fresh in a new headless Edge instance (port 9610, throwaway profile) + http.server (port 8731), both newly started for this task and killed afterward. (2) Ran connectedComponents('D6_primitive1', 1e-5) -- got exactly 13 components (1 body + 6 studs + 6 glyphs), matching the cube's 6-face structure. (3) Computed D6_primitive1's full world matrix via mesh.computeWorldMatrix(true) + mesh.getWorldMatrix() -- confirmed it is NOT identity (verified the exact matrix values, consistent with the task's prior empirical finding of a slight tilt + ~0.89 uniform scale). (4) For each of the 6 glyph components, transformed its LOCAL CENTROID DIRECTION (normalized centroid position, not raw per-vertex normal -- consistent with the D10/D12 centroid-direction method, since this avoids glyph-bevel normal noise) through BABYLON.Vector3.TransformNormal(localDir, worldMatrix) to get the camera-aim direction in WORLD space. (5) Before reading any face, verified alignment: re-transformed the SAME glyph centroid as a world-space COORDINATE via BABYLON.Vector3.TransformCoordinates and re-projected it with BABYLON.Vector3.Project using the camera's actual viewport/transform matrices -- all 6 faces projected to (320.000, 320.000) of the 640x640 canvas (sub-pixel exact, confirmed by scripted output, not eyeballed), i.e. the GEOMETRIC VERIFICATION STEP that the old mapping skipped entirely. (6) Captured each face with Page.captureScreenshot using captureBeyondViewport:true + an explicit clip matching the canvas's actual renderWidth/renderHeight (640x640, confirmed equal to window.innerWidth/innerHeight mismatch was NOT an issue here since clip was taken from engine.getRenderWidth/Height directly). (7) Read each face independently with vision_analyze (neutral stroke-by-stroke description prompt, not a leading question) -- all 6 reads were unambiguous and consistent with the expected digit shapes (1: serif stem+flag; 2: curved-top-to-diagonal-to-base; 3: two stacked lobes; 4: diagonal+crossbar+vertical; 5: flat-top+curve+bowl; 6: hook+closed loop). The -Y face (digit 6) initially rendered too dark to read confidently at default lighting/distance; re-rendered with 2.5x light intensity and a closer camera (distance 2.2 instead of 4) -- re-verified the SAME sub-pixel-exact centroid projection after the re-aim (319.9999, 319.9999) before re-reading, then got an unambiguous '6' read (hook-stroke into closed loop). RESULT: +Y=1, -X=2, -Z=3, +Z=4, +X=5, -Y=6. This EXACTLY matches the task's own empirically-confirmed correct reading (+X=5/-X=2/+Z=4/-Z=3, +Y=1 correct) with the additional -Y=6 now independently confirmed. Complete set {1,2,3,4,5,6} with no repeats -- confirmed. Opposite-pair sums: 1+6=7, 5+2=7, 4+3=7 -- all hold (sum-7 convention, like D8's sum-9 and D12's partial sum-13, but note per the asset-wide anomaly already documented for D8/D12/D20 that sum invariants are NOT guaranteed for this asset family in general; D6 happens to hold them). COMPARISON TABLE (old WRONG mapping vs this corrected mapping, by local axis): +X: old=2, corrected=5 (CHANGED). -X: old=5, corrected=2 (CHANGED). +Y: old=1, corrected=1 (unchanged, was already correct). -Y: old=6, corrected=6 (unchanged, was already correct). +Z: old=3, corrected=4 (CHANGED). -Z: old=4, corrected=3 (CHANGED). LESSON CAPTURED: the sum-7/complete-set invariants cannot by themselves detect a consistent axis-pair swap; only a fresh camera-aim via the current (world-matrix-transformed) method plus explicit centroid-projection verification before reading catches this class of error. This lesson has been added to headless-browser-debugging/references/3d-model-semantic-mapping.md as a generic warning (not D6-specific) for reuse on other projects/assets.
